title: Solar radiation & solar cell optics
subtitle: Where solar energy comes from, how it is spread over photon energies, and how much light actually gets into a solar cell.

skills: Convert nm → m, cm² → m² and eV ↔ J without thinking twice
Use sin and arcsin **in degrees** on your calculator
Evaluate $e^{-x}$ and $\ln x$, and solve $e^{-x} = a$ for $x$
Read a spectrum plot: the area under the curve is a power

concepts.title: Energy, power and energy flow
concepts.summary: Energy is conserved and only converted; power is energy per second; a solar cell taps the radiative energy flow from the hot Sun to cold space.

sources.ref: L1 slides 35–43 (photovoltaic effect, J–V curve preview)

concepts.title: Light as waves and photons
concepts.summary: Light is an electromagnetic wave with wavelength and frequency, and also a stream of photons with energy E = hν = hc/λ.

concepts.title: Thermal radiation: the Sun as a blackbody
concepts.summary: Every object radiates; a blackbody’s spectrum depends only on its temperature (Planck). Its peak follows Wien’s law and its total power σT⁴.

concepts.title: The solar spectrum: irradiance and photon flux
concepts.summary: AM0 and AM1.5 spectra; spectral irradiance vs irradiance (area under the curve); converting power to photon flux; which photons a cell with bandgap E_G can use.

concepts.title: Refraction, reflection and total internal reflection
concepts.summary: Snell’s law bends light at interfaces; the Fresnel equations give how much is reflected; beyond the critical angle light cannot escape.

concepts.title: Anti-reflective coatings and surface texture
concepts.summary: A coating splits one big index step into two smaller ones and, at the right thickness, makes reflections cancel. Texture gives light a second chance and traps it.

concepts.title: Absorption of light: Lambert–Beer
concepts.summary: In an absorbing material the intensity decays exponentially, I = I₀ exp(−αz), with α = 4πκ/λ₀. Weakly absorbed light needs thick layers or light trapping.

notes.text: Instruction 1, Q1: the questions run a–g but the official answers run a–h. Answer “g” (coating thickness λ₀/4n) answers no question, and answer “h” belongs to question g (TIR threshold with a coating). This site follows the question letters.

Instruction 1, Q2(c): the cell-B lines are labelled ‘J_ph,B = q·φ_ph,X’ although the numbers use the absorbed flux of LEDs X+Y (experiment 2) and Y (experiment 3). The numbers are correct; only the label is wrong.

Coatings without interference: instruction 1 Q1(f) uses $R_{tot} = R_1 + R_2$. The book (§10, p. 143) quotes the loss as $1 - (1 - R_1)(1 - R_2)$ (e.g. 22.9 % vs 24.4 % for the ideal interlayer on n = 4.3). Both ignore interference; use the instruction method in exam questions phrased like Q1.

Notation: lecture 1 writes the spectral power density as $P(\lambda)$ and the spectral photon flux density as $\Phi(\lambda)$; the book and formula sheet write $I_{e\lambda}$ and $\Phi_{ph,\lambda}$. Same quantities. This site follows the lecture in explanations and shows both.
Lecture 1, slide 59 defines irradiance as ‘incident power per unit area, per unit wavelength’. ‘Per unit wavelength’ belongs to the *spectral* irradiance only; irradiance is W/m².

AM0 irradiance: lecture 1 slide 57 gives 1353 W/m², the book 1361 W/m², book ex. 5.1 uses 1350 W/m², and the ASTM G173 table used in the diagram integrates to ≈ 1348 W/m² over 280–4000 nm. Use whatever value a question gives.
Book Table 5.1 states that the Earth receives 1.7 × 10¹⁸ W. Lecture 1 slide 43 has 1.7 × 10¹⁷ W, which is correct: 1361 W/m² × π × (6.37 × 10⁶ m)² ≈ 1.7 × 10¹⁷ W.

Lecture 1 slide 60: a yearly irradiation of 1050 kWh/m² corresponds to an average of 120 W/m² and 2.9 equivalent sun hours per day. The slide’s 114 W/m² and 2.7 h/day correspond to 1000 kWh/m² (the book’s value for NL). Small inconsistency, not important for the exam.

Complex refractive index: the book writes ñ = n + iκ (eq. 4.21); book ex. 7.5 (instruction 2) writes ñ = n − ik. Only the sign convention differs; reflectance and $\alpha = 4\pi\kappa/\lambda_0$ are the same.
Book eq. 5.25 gives $\Omega_{Sun} \approx 68.5$ µsr; evaluating eq. 5.24 with the book’s own numbers gives 68.1 µsr. Rounding in the book; irrelevant for the exam.

Diagrams use the ASTM G173-03 AM1.5G/AM0 tables (via pvlib) and the c-Si optical constants of M. A. Green (2008). These are standard reference data, not course material; the course’s own example values (n = 3.57 at 1000 nm, ñ = 3.84 + 0.015i at 650 nm) agree with them.
